metadata.title: Chemical abundances in a high velocity RR Lyrae star near the bulge

notes: No star is eligible. The only analyzed star, MACHO 176.18833.411 (m176), is called a high-velocity RR Lyrae with a space motion of ∼−400 km/s (T:p1-b10), but the authors describe it on an eccentric orbit around the bulge and into the halo (T:p2-b1) and state that it has completed many orbits around the bulge (T:p7-b6). They do not explicitly identify it as unbound from the Milky Way or state that it satisfies a Galactic escape criterion. The paper's escape-velocity comparison (V_escape = 231.2 km/s versus V_expansion ∼90 km/s; T:p4-b9, T:p4-b11) concerns whether material remains bound to the stellar surface, not Galactic binding. The HVS designation is therefore only a velocity label. Other high-velocity stars and samples are cited as background, not studied here.
